text_summary: Says a cloud start hook can lack CLAUDE_CODE_EXECPATH, so the claude binary is found through PATH; the binary is read by anchor strings.
text: - Source: the installed binary, read in-process. It is the file at env `CLAUDE_CODE_EXECPATH`. When that variable is missing or cannot be read, it is `claude` on the env `PATH`, followed through its link to the real file: cloud start hooks can lack the variable (seen in 2.1.317). The binary is read by anchor strings: setting keys, env names, a flag name (`tengu_amber_rokovoko`) and a property name (`maxOutputTokens`). Never a minified name. A minified name is only followed to its own declaration, `var|let|const NAME=<number>` or `,NAME=<number>`: the nearest one before the anchor, else the nearest after it. A bare `NAME=<number>` elsewhere is an assignment and is skipped. The blocking margin is the identifier in the last `)-NAME:void 0,` match within 2500 bytes before the `autocompact_buffer` id. The output reserve is the identifier after `.maxOutputTokens,` that ends in `)`.
